label: D1 after an a1 trial that went rarely to S2 and was unrewarded
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO or D2), almost only when the reward input is 0 (99% of mass), and almost only after the previous choice was a1 (80% of mass; prev_action a2 gives 1.7%) that took the rare transition to S2 (prev_common==0, rate 9% vs 0.1% after common). This is the rare-unrewarded a1 case, where a model-based agent should repeat a1, and the agent does go on to choose a1 (99.9% of mass has action a1, and the policy logit is moderately pro-a1 at 2.8 to 8). The observed-only predicate D1 & prev_reward==0 & prev_action==1 & prev_common==0 gets dev F1 0.78 (P 0.80, R 0.76). Most of its misses are on the first trial of the window, where the previous trial is outside the window (prev_action == -1). To cover those I added a clause that uses the agent own upcoming choice (action==1, marked FUTURE but computed by the agent, not a random outcome). That gives dev F1 0.81, mass recall 0.97, and is what I recorded. Because of that proxy, precision drops at the window start. It also fires weakly after some common-a1-unrewarded trials. It does not fire on rewarded D1s or before a2 choices. Activations are larger in later episode trials and when value is low to mid. I did not check finer magnitude structure.

issues: The explanation says it 'fires weakly after some common-a1-unrewarded trials', which is false. D1 & prev_reward==0 & prev_action==1 & prev_common==1 has zero active steps (precision 0, n_predicted 22104). All 943 dev firings outside the a1-rare case come after a2-common trials, which also reach S2 (rate about 3%, 1.7% of mass). The rest of the reward-input-1 mass (0.8%) comes after a1-rare-rewarded trials (rate 7.7%). So every firing follows a trial that reached S2.

Within the core class (D1, unrewarded, previous trial a1 then rare), precision is about 0.80 and depends on episode time: 0.92 for ep_bucket 5 and 0.67 earlier. It is also near 0.97 when value >= 7.73, but that bin has little recall. This is gain modulation, not a separate counterexample class.

The FUTURE clause (prev_action==-1 & action==1) only patches the window boundary: it has precision 0.48 and recall 0.17. Without it, the observed-only predicate scores test F1 0.772 (P 0.79, R 0.75, mass recall 0.79), against 0.795 for the recorded predicate. The whole gap comes from the window's first trial, where history is missing. The label is already phrased in observed terms.

Confirmed claims: fires only at D1 (GO and D2: 0 active). 99.1% of mass has reward input 0. 80.4% of mass follows a1-rare trials. Firing rate is 9.0% after a rare transition and 0.14% after a common one. 99.9% of mass precedes an a1 choice, and 99.6% of mass falls where the choice logit is in [2.78, 8.07). Test misses carry only 2.8% of mass. The test false positives are mainly the first-trial clause plus the precision dilution described above.
